paragraphs: Here's what I see, friend. Saul went from hunting followers of Jesus to telling people, "He is the Son of God." (Acts 9:20) And folks in Damascus were astounded, because they knew who he used to be (Acts 9:21). Nobody walks in the door with a clean résumé. Jesus takes people as they are and changes where they're headed.

Now look at what following Jesus cost Saul. A plot to kill him in Damascus. Frightened disciples in Jerusalem, who were "not believing that he was a disciple." (Acts 9:26) Another attempt on his life from the Grecian Jews (Acts 9:29). I think that's a LOT for a brand new believer, and the passage doesn't hide it. Speaking boldly for Jesus can bring pushback, and Saul kept going anyway (Acts 9:28).

But Saul never did it alone, and that's the part I love. Disciples lowered him in a basket (Acts 9:25), Barnabas stood up for him when everybody else kept their distance (Acts 9:27), and the brothers got him safely on his way (Acts 9:30). Then the church had "a time of peace," living in "the encouragement of the Holy Spirit." (Acts 9:31) So be a Barnabas, baker, and let a Barnabas help you too, because the story isn't over and Saul's journey keeps going.
